coordinates.locator: Nominatim result 1: OSM relation 20818263 (Savannah River Site boundary), lat/lon fields
coordinates.note: Centroid of the OSM boundary of the whole site (bounding box roughly 40 km across), not the P Reactor building. Geocoder, so campus-grade only (A17); no fetched source gives coordinates for P Area.

name: Savannah River Site
notes: The point is the centroid of the OpenStreetMap boundary of the whole site, so it can lie tens of kilometres from P Reactor. A surveyed or official coordinate for P Area would replace it; none was found in the sources consulted on 2026-10-26.

summary.plain: The Savannah River Site, a very large U.S. Department of Energy reservation in South Carolina on the Savannah River, where the P Reactor stood in which Cowan and Reines detected the neutrino in 1956.
summary.technical: Whole-site point for the 310-square-mile Savannah River Site (Aiken, Barnwell and Allendale counties, South Carolina). The Cowan–Reines detector sat in an underground room of the P Reactor building, which is not separately geolocated by any source consulted.
